about: The bucket and the pre-accept predicate, as a truth table. Published for the same reason the comparator is: the field contract was pinned once and two tracks still drifted on the thing the fields feed. clause_order is the strict precedence; cases drive items.security_tier(), items.pre_accept_bars(), validate_items.compute_initial_bucket(), assemble.apply_pre_accept() and converge.initial_pre_accept() directly, in the validator's order (tier, bars, bucket), and test_items.py asserts clause_order's length equals the number of return statements in the function, so a clause added without a fixture row is caught. A case's `stored_tier` stands for a tier the validator stored that the harness must NOT recompute (the view default). expect.tier / expect.priority are null for a tool that is not G-SEC.
d2_routing: clause-2b guard (orchestrator ruling, overriding the spec's variants A and B): a barred security-only tool falls through to security_mixed — never to attention (A), and never left in security_auto with a cleared checkbox (B). security_mixed already renders an expanded card with an 'affects this setup' badge and correct counters; anything downstream of finalize_tool desyncs the Overview tiles. Since CONTRACT 4 D2 governs every tool that is NOT G-SEC — including one whose only security content is not a positively identified fix.
g_sec_routing: a version-source tool with a positively identified security fix (security.nature == fix, grounded by I-21) or a vendor-declared unread security release is G-SEC: security_tier(view) computes its display priority (P0-P3) and its acceptance holds once, the validator stores it, and clause 2 routes it — an accepted tier (P1, P2, P3) to security_auto, P0 and held to security_mixed. D2's elevated bar and the reaches limb do not apply to it; the priority panel is the visibility D2 asked for. enum-invalid and container-unreadable bar every tool, G-SEC or not (R7).
clause_order: 0. content_losing(view) is non-empty -> attention   [D1 - above the source clause on purpose]
1. source in NON_VERSION_SOURCES -> routine if expected else attention
2. security_tier(view) is not None -> security_auto if the stored tier is valid and tier in ACCEPTED_TIERS (P1, P2, P3) else security_mixed   [G-SEC - P0 and held tools are never in the auto strip]

2b. has_security and security_only and impact == "none" and version_delta not in (major, unknown) and runnable and not pre_accept_bars(view) -> security_auto   [pre-G-SEC, unchanged: D2/E3 - a barred tool falls through to security_mixed]
4. risk_level elevated, or config needs_attention, or an edit/structural suggestion (items.needs_a_decision), or not runnable -> attention
pre_accept: sug is baseline AND auto_runnable AND items.accepts_baseline(tool) — one predicate for assembly and convergence, reading security_tier (key required: null or an object), pre_accept_bars (key required: the EXPORTED bars, never recomputed), the bucket, risk_level and forced_conservative. Not G-SEC (security_tier null): bucket != "attention" AND risk_level == "low" AND not content_losing AND pre_accept_bars == [] AND not forced_conservative. G-SEC: the tier is valid AND tier in ACCEPTED_TIERS AND not content_losing AND pre_accept_bars == [] AND not forced_conservative. A malformed tier ({} included) is never accepted. The bars and the tier are the VALIDATOR'S, copied by finalize_tool — assembly never recomputes them from assembled items, which can hold synthesized reaching security items the bucket never saw

pre_accept_bars.required-edit: G-SEC P0: an action suggestion reads required (I-22) — the upgrade does not work here without it
pre_accept_bars.pinned: G-SEC P0: the tool is pinned; the fix cannot land
pre_accept_bars.incompatible-unfixed: G-SEC P0: an incompatible item no required edit serves
pre_accept_bars.security-item-risk: G-SEC hold: a security item (tag or block) whose local.effect is risk — the upgrade adds a security risk here (§7.27)
pre_accept_bars.watch-hit: any item carrying a watch_hit — a watch item exists to be told about, and one that fires into an auto-accepted card is inert (E3); every tool
pre_accept_bars.enum-invalid: any tier-input enum present and outside its vocabulary — severity, local.direction, local.effect, security.nature, evidence role, suggestion kind, requirement, config_status.state. The renamed and widened local-enum-invalid: a one-character drift ("reachs", "risks") on a real CVE item removes the reaches-item bar and the impact signal at once, and E-ENUM-INVALID alone bars nothing. An unverifiable claim fails closed here as everywhere in this contract. Every tool, G-SEC or not (R7)
pre_accept_bars.container-unreadable: an item's local/security/change/watch_hit present and not an object, tags present and not an array, or an action suggestion's serves present and not an array — `local: "risk"` used to read as no local claim at all. Every tool (R7)
pre_accept_bars.research-incomplete: G-SEC hold: the checker reported research_error (R3)
pre_accept_bars.not-runnable: G-SEC hold: no runnable upgrade — accepted would claim a run the skill cannot make (R3)
pre_accept_bars.forced-conservative: G-SEC hold: written by the applier on a degraded-gate tool (R3)
pre_accept_bars.tier-uncomputed: the view default, or a malformed stored tier — never observed unless the tier function could not run on the final view
pre_accept_bars.reaches-item: NOT G-SEC only: an item that ITSELF carries security content (the security tag, or a security block) with local.direction == "reaches" — the measured case: cask:wireshark-app's reaching item IS the security item. Never any reaching item, and never any reaching item on a security tool: the measurement was taken on security items only, and a re-widened predicate quietly un-compresses the routine population
